title: Pleasant closeness need not become possession
meaning: Your attention can bring pleasure when wanting to hold closeness does not claim another person’s later response.
text: Welcome tenderness can coexist with a need to secure it permanently. In the physical position of Anahata, the Lovers express care through freely offered personal attention. The Devil in energy brings a motive of indispensability, wanting to hold connection so firmly that it cannot be postponed. The Empress in emotions offers pleasure in received warmth and comfort nearby. The pleasant response can be real even while an extra expectation begins forming behind it. Today’s agreement does not prescribe a later answer.

For example, you offer to sit together beneath a blanket and put on a familiar film. The invitation is willingly accepted, making an ordinary evening particularly comfortable. **Accepted tenderness does not give you a right to all later attention.** After a while the other person may want to read separately. That continuation does not cancel pleasure in the meeting. Care stays personal when maintaining comfort does not require compulsory presence to prove the invitation’s value or the importance of whoever wanted company.

Comfort becomes restrictive when a separate wish demands even greater gratitude. Someone is reminded how thoughtfully everything was arranged, making departure seem ungrateful. Received pleasure becomes a debt. Warmth remains nourishing when attention can be willingly accepted and the meeting calmly ended. A free response can return precisely because it did not have to defend against a concealed claim of possession.
